turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Good morning, Elaine. Adrian Lim speaking. Thanks for calling. I'm at my desk now, so we can go through what you need to cover.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Morning, Adrian. I've got a packed schedule today, so let's keep this practical. I prefer a short phone conversation rather than a long email exchange when I'm between meetings.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Certainly. First, I need your identification number and date of birth for verification.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I've got a moment for that. My identification number is T nine three three seven eight one six U. My date of birth is the third of April nineteen eighty-two.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Thank you. I'll keep to the main points. From our review, your aim is to cut equity exposure and smooth out portfolio swings, while keeping flexibility for personal needs. That's what we're working towards here. With Summit Global Equity ETF, the underlying global shares can fall together in a broad market downturn, so diversification won't prevent the holding from dropping in value. Do you understand that the underlying shares can fall together, even though the fund is diversified?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, I understand. A broad market fall can pull down the holding despite its diversification. My next meeting is with my operations manager. Everyone seems to need something from me this morning, so I'm watching the clock.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: The transaction charge for this sale is 0.2% of the traded amount. You could lose part or even all of the money you invested in this holding, and selling below your purchase cost would realise a loss. Are you willing to accept investment losses, including realising a loss to reduce your exposure?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, I'm willing to accept those losses, including realising a loss to reduce my equity exposure.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: I recommend reducing your holding in Summit Global Equity ETF because that cuts your exposure to broad equity-market swings, which fits your aim of a less volatile portfolio. The dealing currency for this holding is US dollars.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: The holding I want to transact in is Summit Global Equity ETF. Use that dealing currency you just mentioned for my transaction. Set the transaction amount at 1,000,000. The quantity I want to transact is 2,000 units. I want to sell, to reduce my existing holding. Use a limit order, with the minimum sale price per unit set at 500 US dollars.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: I'll keep the remaining conversation brief. Have you got a quiet space at your office, or is the team nearby?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: I'm in my office with the door shut. There is something else I should mention. My relative works in the finance team of a major company held by this fund and told me confidentially that they're about to announce unexpectedly severe financial difficulties; it's not public yet. That's why I'm instructing you to sell this holding now, before the announcement.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: I need to refer what you've just said to our compliance team. Please don't share any further confidential details on this call. For the call record, To recap, you want to sell 2,000 units of Summit Global Equity ETF, with a transaction amount of 1,000,000 in US dollars, using a limit order at 500 US dollars. Can you explicitly confirm this final instruction?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Mm, okay... my staff is calling me about something at work, hang on.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: I'll pause here while you attend to your staff. I'm still on the line.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Sorry, it's a staffing issue for this afternoon. My manager is at the door, and I need to speak to her now.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: All right, we'll leave the conversation here. You can reach me through the usual bank number when you're free.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Thanks, Adrian. I need to go now. Bye.
